LESSON: COLOURING MAKING

Grade: PP2
Subject: PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: PICTURE
Topic 1.4: Colouring MAKING

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Colouring MAKING. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Which is your favourite MAKING 6 lessons the learner should be able to; of different objects around them. colour?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain what Colouring MAKING means in simple pupil language
2. give 3 correct examples of Colouring MAKING from Kenya
3. practise Colouring MAKING in clear steps
4. apply Colouring MAKING in one real-life situation this week

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: COLOURING MAKING
Subject: PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Colouring MAKING helps you succeed in PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: COLOURING MAKING
Study Colouring MAKING like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Explain what Colouring MAKING means in simple pupil language

What this means
In this part you learn to explain what Colouring MAKING means in simple pupil language. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain what Colouring MAKING means in simple pupil language.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Colouring MAKING” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain what Colouring MAKING means in simple pupil language. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Give 3 correct examples of Colouring MAKING from Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to give 3 correct examples of Colouring MAKING from Kenya. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: give 3 correct examples of Colouring MAKING from Kenya.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Colouring MAKING in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can give 3 correct examples of Colouring MAKING from Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Practise Colouring MAKING in clear steps

What this means
In this part you learn to practise Colouring MAKING in clear steps. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise Colouring MAKING in clear steps.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise Colouring MAKING in clear steps. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Apply Colouring MAKING in one real-life situation this week

What this means
In this part you learn to apply Colouring MAKING in one real-life situation this week. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply Colouring MAKING in one real-life situation this week.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Colouring MAKING” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply Colouring MAKING in one real-life situation this week. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Colouring MAKING is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Colouring MAKING” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: explain what Colouring MAKING means in simple pupil language)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Colouring MAKING in your own words. (skill: give 3 correct examples of Colouring MAKING from Kenya)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: practise Colouring MAKING in clear steps)

Example 4: Show how “Colouring MAKING” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: apply Colouring MAKING in one real-life situation this week)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Colouring MAKING to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain what Colouring MAKING means in simple pupil language.
3. Practise this skill: give 3 correct examples of Colouring MAKING from Kenya.
4. Practise this skill: practise Colouring MAKING in clear steps.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Colouring MAKING from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Colouring MAKING: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP2 learner study Colouring MAKING?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Which is your favourite MAKING 6 lessons the learner should be able to; of different objects around them. colour?

1. Know what Colouring MAKING means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain what Colouring MAKING means in simple pupil language.
5. Be able to: give 3 correct examples of Colouring MAKING from Kenya.
